answer: A sybil-resistant economy can treat every agent as a vertex in a shared trust graph, where reputation flows only from identities that have staked a deposit. A newcomer may wander in freely, but it cannot earn weight until others with staked reputation vouch for it, and those vouchers lose their stake if the newcomer cheats. An umber tint of suspicion falls on accounts with no stake and no endorsers: they can observe, but cannot transact at full value. Creating a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand stakes, which makes the attack unprofitable while honest newcomers can still join.
